did_you_know.text: Did you know? The phrase “Lech lecha” literally means “go for yourself,” or simply “set out”; repeating “go” emphasizes the force of the command.
Did you know? In Biblical Hebrew, “nefesh” can mean a living person. Thus, “the people they made in Haran” is often understood as people who joined Abram’s household, not people he created.
Did you know? Shechem was an important city in the central hill country, roughly near today’s Nablus. It lies between Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal.
Did you know? “The Negev” was not only the name of the desert within modern Israel’s borders. In the Bible, it means “the dry region” or “the southern region,” and its boundaries varied by period.
Did you know? Egypt was a natural destination during famine in Canaan because the Nile provided a more reliable water source than rivers and streams dependent on rainfall.
Did you know? The list also includes camels, valuable animals for carrying people and goods. It portrays Abram’s wealth and the size of his household.
Did you know? The word “plagues” is a general term for afflictions or harmful blows. The verse does not specify exactly what illness or injury affected Pharaoh and his household.
